syntax_forms: ALTER TABLE [IF EXISTS] table_name CLUSTER BY (column, ...)
ALTER TABLE [IF EXISTS] table_name RENAME TO new_table_name
alter_table.summary: Change a table's clustering columns or its name.
alter_table.documentation: CLUSTER BY records the columns a catalog-backed table is sorted by, in priority order. RENAME TO renames the relation and may move it between collections.
alter_table.notes: One operation per statement. CLUSTER BY takes column names, not expressions. RENAME TO cannot cross workspaces. Every other ALTER TABLE operation (ADD COLUMN, DROP COLUMN, ...) is rejected at plan time.

alter_view.documentation: The logical planner stores the replacement query and view metadata.

syntax_forms: ALTER WORKSPACE workspace SET property TO value
alter_workspace.summary: Set a protection property on a workspace itself.
alter_workspace.documentation: Sets one of the properties in WORKSPACE_PROPERTIES on the workspace's catalog entry. Both are protections and both default to ON: deletion_protection refuses deletion of the workspace, egress_protection refuses automated copies of its data into another workspace. Values are ON/OFF (TRUE/FALSE accepted).
alter_workspace.notes: Names a workspace, never a relation within one; a qualified name is rejected. An unrecognised property name is rejected at plan time. Requires a connector with a catalog to store the property in.

analyze_table.documentation: Requires the TABLE keyword and a table name.

comment_on.documentation: The SQL rewriter normalizes TABLE and VIEW to EXTENSION before parsing.

create_collection.summary: Create a collection inside a workspace.
create_collection.documentation: The SQL rewriter turns this into CREATE SCHEMA, which the parser has a grammar for; CREATE SCHEMA spelled directly lands on the same builder.
create_collection.notes: The name is always two parts, workspace.collection; a bare or three-part name is rejected at plan time. Creating a collection is optional - one comes into existence with the first relation placed in it.

syntax_forms: CREATE [OR REPLACE] MATERIALIZED VIEW view_name AS query
create_materialized_view.documentation: Planned as CTAS plus registration: the query runs now and its result is written as a backing table, and refresh triggers are registered on every source table so commits to them re-run the query.
create_materialized_view.notes: IF NOT EXISTS and explicit column lists are rejected; use CREATE OR REPLACE, and name columns with AS in the SELECT.

syntax_forms: CREATE TABLE [IF NOT EXISTS] table_name (column_name column_type [NOT NULL], ...)
CREATE [OR REPLACE] TABLE table_name AS query
create_table.summary: Create a table, optionally from a query result.
create_table.documentation: The explicit-column form builds a RelationSchema, resolving each declared type exactly as a CAST target resolves. The AS query form (CTAS) plans the SELECT and attaches an Insert sink, deriving the target schema at bind time.
create_table.notes: OR REPLACE applies to the CTAS form only. EXTERNAL, TEMPORARY, TRANSIENT, VOLATILE and ICEBERG are rejected, as is a column list on a CTAS.

create_view.documentation: The query body is stored for later planning when the view is referenced.
create_view.notes: Supports OR REPLACE and optional column lists.

distinct.documentation: Distinct can be pushed down in some planner paths and appears as a logical plan node.
distinct.notes: DISTINCT ON is rendered but may be planner-specific.

drop_collection.documentation: The SQL rewriter turns this into DROP SCHEMA; plan_drop routes the Schema object type to a DropCollection node.
drop_collection.notes: The collection must already be empty - the drop never cascades. CASCADE, RESTRICT and PURGE are rejected rather than accepted and ignored.

drop_materialized_view.documentation: Builds the same DropRelation node as DROP TABLE, flagged so execution routes to the connector's materialized-view drop, which also removes the refresh triggers from every source table.
drop_materialized_view.notes: DROP TABLE against a materialized view is rejected, and this statement against a plain table is rejected, each pointing at the other.

drop_table.documentation: Supports dropping one or more tables with optional IF EXISTS.
drop_table.notes: CASCADE, RESTRICT and PURGE are rejected rather than accepted and ignored.

syntax_forms: DROP TRIGGER [IF EXISTS] trigger_name ON table_name
drop_trigger.summary: Remove a refresh trigger from a table.
drop_trigger.documentation: Synthesized by the planner's pre-parse interception; the dialect has no native sqlparser grammar for trigger statements.
drop_trigger.notes: The table is required: trigger names are unique only per dataset, and the table is the permission target. The materialized view stays queryable but stops refreshing.

drop_view.documentation: Supports dropping one or more views with optional IF EXISTS and CASCADE/RESTRICT flags.
drop_view.notes: Only DROP VIEW is accepted by this planner path.

explain.documentation: Supports textual and Mermaid output formats.
explain.notes: GRAPHVIZ is normalized to MERMAID in the planner.

from.documentation: The planner builds scans, joins, subqueries, and function datasets from FROM sources.
from.notes: Implicit cross joins are supported through relation lists.

group_by.documentation: Supports the GROUP BY ALL rewrite path via wildcard projection handling.
group_by.notes: The logical planner rewrites wildcard grouping into explicit projection columns.

having.documentation: HAVING predicates are preserved in the logical plan and later optimized.
having.notes: Aggregate references in HAVING are handled by planner rewrite paths.

insert.documentation: The VALUES form feeds a VALUES function dataset into an Insert sink; the SELECT form plans the query and attaches the sink to its Exit node.
insert.notes: INSERT OVERWRITE is rejected; TRUNCATE the table first. An explicit column list must name every column in the target relation.

limit.documentation: The planner also carries OFFSET together with LIMIT in limit_clause metadata.
limit.notes: Used by file-pruning and pushdown optimizers.

offset.documentation: OFFSET is parsed as part of the limit clause.

order_by.documentation: The planner rejects literal ORDER BY expressions and supports alias-aware rewriting.
order_by.notes: Order-by columns may be injected before projection.

refresh_materialized_view.summary: Rebuild a materialized view from its defining SELECT.
refresh_materialized_view.documentation: Re-runs the view's current definition and replaces its contents, reusing the CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE AS write path so the swap is atomic. Views also refresh automatically when a source table takes a user write; this statement is for rebuilding after a failed refresh or a redefinition.
refresh_materialized_view.notes: Takes no options. Refused if the target is not a materialized view. A materialized view is not a table: CTAS, INSERT, TRUNCATE and ALTER TABLE are all refused against one.

select.documentation: SELECT drives the main query planning path.
select.notes: Supports DISTINCT and set operations via the query planner.

set.documentation: The logical planner has a dedicated SET node for variable assignment.
set.notes: This is a statement-level capability, not a clause.

show_columns.documentation: The planner creates SHOW COLUMNS nodes and optionally applies filters.
show_columns.notes: Filtering SHOW COLUMNS is currently rejected.

show_create.summary: Show CREATE SQL for an object.
show_create.documentation: Handled as a SHOW node with object metadata.

show_triggers.summary: List the refresh triggers attached to a table.
show_triggers.documentation: Reached through the parser's generic SHOW catch-all and planned as a filtered scan of the workspace's information_schema.triggers.
show_triggers.notes: Bare SHOW TRIGGERS is rejected - there is no session default workspace to enumerate; name the table with FOR, or query information_schema.triggers.

top.documentation: Rejected by the planner; use LIMIT instead.
top.notes: The logical planner emits an UnsupportedSyntaxError.

truncate_table.summary: Remove every row from a table, keeping the table and its schema.
truncate_table.documentation: Builds a TruncateRelation node carrying the relation name.
truncate_table.notes: The TABLE keyword is required, and a single table name is accepted per statement.

union.documentation: The logical planner supports UNION and applies DISTINCT unless ALL is specified.
union.notes: Set operations are routed through the Union logical node.

where.documentation: WHERE conditions are rewritten into filters and may be optimized or pushed down.
where.notes: Predicate pushdown and boolean simplification operate on WHERE clauses.

with.documentation: CTEs are extracted before query planning and tracked as subplans.
with.notes: Used for recursive and non-recursive CTE support.
